'''''Centaurium tenuiflorum''''', the '''slender centaury''', is a species of annual herb in the family [[Gentianaceae]]. They have a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves. Individuals can grow to 17 cm tall.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Centaurium tenuiflorum (Hoffmgg. \u0026 Link) Fritsch - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/6856176|access-date=2022-02-04|website=eol.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mifsud|first=Stephen|date=2002-08-23|title=Centaurium tenuiflorum (Slender Centaury) : MaltaWildPlants.com - the online Flora of the Maltese Islands.|url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/GENT/Centaurium_tenuiflorum.php|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.maltawildplants.com|language=en-us}}</ref> It is native to the [[Mediterranean basin]], Western Asia to the [[Transcaucasus]], Iran, and western Himalayas, [[Macaronesia]], [[Great Britain]], the [[Crimean Peninsula]], Chad, and [[Socotra]]. 

The species was first described as ''Erythraea tenuiflora'' by [[Johann Centurius Hoffmannsegg]] and [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link]] in 1813. In 1907 [[Karl Fritsch]] reassigned it to genus ''[[Centaurium]]'' as ''Centaurium tenuiflorum''.<ref name = powo/>

==Subspecies==
Four subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Centaurium tenuiflorum'' subsp. ''acutiflorum'' {{small|(Schott) Zeltner}} – Mediterranean basin to Crimea, Iran, Transcaucasus, and western Himalayas
*''Centaurium tenuiflorum'' subsp. ''anglicum'' {{small|T.C.G.Rich & McVeigh}} – southern Great Britain
*''Centaurium tenuiflorum'' subsp. ''tenuiflorum'' – Mediterranean basin, Chad, Azores, Canary Islands, Madeira, and Socotra
*''Centaurium tenuiflorum'' subsp. ''viridense'' {{small|(Bolle) O.Erikss., A.Hansen & Sunding}} – [[Cape Verde Islands]]
